info.description: Generated from the API route schemas by `pnpm gen:api`. Do not edit by hand.

mfaEnabled.description: Whether sign-in asks for an authenticator code.

activeTenant.description: Null until a user with several hospitals picks one.

policy.description: Null when there is no active tenant.

needsPassword.description: False when this person already has an account: they only accept.

secret.description: Base32, for typing into an authenticator by hand.

recoveryCodes.description: One-time codes. Returned this once and never again.

primary.description: Brand colour as six-digit hex. Must read as text on a white background (contrast of at least 4.5:1); the web app falls back to its default colour otherwise.

logoUrl.description: https or same-origin URL of the hospital logo (SVG or WebP, at most 50 kB).

address.description: Postal address, printed on the letterhead. May hold line breaks.

phone.description: Phone number, printed on the letterhead.

registrationNumber.description: The hospital's registration or licence number as a clinical establishment, printed on the letterhead.

features.description: Module flags. A module that is absent is off.

idleTimeoutMinutes.description: A session with no activity for this long ends. The web app warns shortly before and signs the user out. Absent means the app default.

status.description: A suspended hospital keeps its data but its staff cannot use the app. Tenant-scoped routes answer 403 tenant_suspended.

Invite.description: An invitation that has been emailed. The link is not returned.

StaffMember.description: Someone who works at the hospital, or has been invited to. For a member `id` is the user id; for an invitation it is the invitation id.

StaffPage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

PatientSummary.description: A patient as shown in a list: compact, no clinical data.

phone.description: Masked to its last four digits for a caller without patient.contact:read.

PatientRecord.description: A registered patient with the details captured at registration. Email and address are left out for a caller without patient.contact:read.

version.description: Goes up by one each time the record changes. Send it back as expectedVersion when changing the record.

PatientUpdate.description: The version the change is based on, and the fields to change. Null clears an optional field. The MRN never changes.

expectedVersion.description: The version of the record the change was made from. If the record has changed since, the request is refused with 409 conflict and nothing is changed.

PatientDuplicateMatch.description: A possible duplicate, masked by the server: enough to recognise the person, not to read their details. No id.

Department.description: A department of one hospital. Holds no patient data.

version.description: Counts the changes. Sent back as expectedVersion.

DepartmentPage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

Doctor.description: A doctor profile: a staff member of one hospital, in one department. Holds no patient data.

active.description: False once the doctor no longer practises here, or while their membership of the hospital is deactivated: kept on old records, not offered for new ones.

qualifications.description: Recognised degrees as printed after the name, e.g. "MBBS, MD (General Medicine)".

registrationCouncil.description: The council that gave the registration number: the NMC or a state medical council.

consultationMinutes.description: The usual length of one appointment.

DoctorAvailability.description: Regular weekly working hours. A day without a session is a day off.

ServicePrice.description: What a service costs on one price list from one date. A price is never edited: a new one takes over from its own date.

amountMinor.description: In the minor unit of the hospital's currency.

effectiveFrom.description: A calendar date at the hospital.

effectiveTo.description: The last day it applies. Absent while no later price follows.

Service.description: Something the hospital can charge for. Holds no patient data. code.description: The service's identity on bills. Never changes.

taxClass.description: Which tax rate applies, as a class. The rate of each class is the hospital's tax setting, so a change of rate does not touch the services.

modality.description: The equipment an imaging service is performed on, which sorts radiology’s worklist. Only a service of the category imaging has one.

type.description: A medicine, or a consumable such as gloves or a syringe.

genericName.description: The generic name of a medicine, or what a consumable is.

reorderLevel.description: Stock at or below this many units is low. Absent: no level set.

LabTest.description: A test or a panel the laboratory offers: what it is, how it is collected and how its result is read. Holds no patient data.

code.description: The test's identity on orders and reports. Never changes.

kind.description: A single test, or a panel: a named set of tests ordered together (a lipid profile). A panel has components and no result of its own.

resultType.description: How a result is recorded: a number against a reference range, or text (positive, negative, a description). For a panel it means nothing.

unit.description: The unit of a numeric result: g/dL.

container.description: What the sample is collected in.

turnaroundHours.description: How long a result usually takes from collection.

serviceName.description: The name of the linked service, when there is one. The name alone is shown to everyone who may read the test, by decision; nothing else of the service (a price, a tax class) is ever added here.

components.description: The tests of a panel. Empty for a single test.

LabAge.description: An age as it is written: a value with its unit. Never turned into a count of days: a patient reaches it on the calendar day that lies that long after the date of birth, so leap years and the lengths of months are respected. At most 150 years, in any unit.

LabRange.description: What is normal for one sex in one span of age: from `ageFrom`, included (the day the patient reaches it), until `ageUntil`, not included (that day belongs to the next range). No `ageUntil`: no upper age.

sex.description: Whom the row is for. A row for one sex is used before a row for any.

low.description: The lowest normal value. Absent: no lower limit.

high.description: The highest normal value. Absent: no upper limit.

criticalLow.description: At or below this the result is critical. Only with `low`, and below it.

criticalHigh.description: At or above this the result is critical. Only with `high`, and above it.

LabRangeResolved.description: `range` is absent when no row covers that age and sex.

BedCategory.description: A class of bed (general ward, private room, intensive care), which decides what a day in it is charged as. The charge itself is posted by the admissions module from the linked service, at the price in force that day. An admission keeps the category and the service of its bed as they were when the patient was given it, so a change made here applies to stays that start after it.

serviceName.description: The name of the linked service, when there is one. The name alone is shown to everyone who may read wards, by decision; nothing else of the service (a price, a tax class) is ever added here.

bedCount.description: The beds in use that have this category.

Code.description: A diagnosis code (ICD-10) or a procedure code. Reference data shared by every hospital, so it carries no tenant; only `favourite` is the hospital’s own.

code.description: As it is written: A09, E11.9.

body.description: The text of a template: the rich text document of the app (paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes and marks), never HTML. Reduced to that allowlist on the way in. Placeholders are plain text in double braces, `{{patient.name}}`. A placeholder is recognised only inside one run of text, for the check and for filling alike: one that is split by formatting (half of it bold) is neither checked nor ever filled, by any part of the system. Names are trimmed and case-sensitive. A value is filled in as text and is never read for placeholders again.

ImportBatch.description: Records of one kind loaded from a file. It holds counts and codes, never a value of a row.

status.description: staging: rows are being sent. checking: the dry run is running. checked: it has run, and the batch can be written when problemCount is 0. queued, running: being written. committed: every row was written. failed: nothing was written. cancelled: given up, or left unfinished for a week.

doneCount.description: Rows checked while checking, rows written while running.

failure.description: Why nothing was written, as a code: rows_refused (see the problems), permission_withdrawn, write_failed, expired.

ImportRowsUpload.description: Rows of the file, as many requests as it takes. A line sent twice is kept as it was first sent.

fields.description: The fields of the kind the columns of the file were mapped to, in the order of `values`. Each at most once.

values.description: The text of each field of `fields`. An empty text is no value.

ImportProblem.description: Never the value that was refused.

code.description: What is wrong. Of one field: required, not_a_whole_number, not_yes_or_no, not_allowed, not_a_date, not_an_amount, too_many_decimals, invalid, not_found, out_of_range, too_few_digits, not_an_email. Of a row: duplicate_in_file, or the code its create route answers with (drug_exists, service_code_taken, lab_test_code_taken, patient_possible_duplicate, validation_failed).

A caller who may neither enter nor verify results (labResult:enter or labResult:verify at the scope `all`) gets verified results only, and `awaitingVerification` names the tests whose result is still to verify. Every result given is audited. Requires labResult:read with the scope `all` and the laboratory feature flag.

200.description: The results of a lab order: those of its sample that is not rejected, and what they are entered for. No sample yet: no results.

post.description: Enters results of a received sample: some or all of the tests of its order (the test, or each test of the panel), each once (400 otherwise). A test that is not of the order is 422 `unknown_test`, one that has a result already 409 `already_resulted` (correct it instead), a number that is not one 422 `invalid_number`. A sample not received, and an order cancelled or completed, are 409 `invalid_transition`. A sample with a partner laboratory whose report is not back is 409 `with_partner` (#94). A number is read against the range for the patient’s sex and age on the day the sample was collected, which the result keeps. The first result moves the order in progress. A critical result emits `lab.critical_value`. The Idempotency-Key header is required: a repeat enters nothing and answers with the results as they are now. Requires labResult:enter and the laboratory feature flag. Audited.

parameters.name: idempotency-key
parameters.description: A unique value (such as a UUID) chosen by the client, required: a request without one is refused (400). Repeating the request with the same key returns the first result instead of doing the work again; the same key with a different request is refused (422 `idempotency_key_reuse`).

201.description: The results of a lab order: those of its sample that is not rejected, and what they are entered for. No sample yet: no results.

post.description: Verifies results of a sample, as the verifier read them: each must be a result of the sample (422 `unknown_result`) that is current and not yet verified (409 `conflict`: corrected or verified meanwhile, read again). The person who entered a result may verify it. Once every test of the order has a current result and all are verified, the order is completed (emitting `order.completed`) and `lab.result_verified` is emitted; a correction verified after that emits `lab.result_verified` again. Refused for a cancelled order (409 `invalid_transition`). The Idempotency-Key header is required: a repeat verifies nothing and answers with the results as they are now. Requires labResult:verify and the laboratory feature flag. Audited.

It is entered, so it needs verifying again; the order stays as it is, completed included. A result is corrected once (409 `already_amended`): a later correction corrects the correction. Refused for a cancelled order (409 `invalid_transition`). A critical result emits `lab.critical_value`. The Idempotency-Key header is required: a repeat answers with the correction as it is now. Requires labResult:enter and the laboratory feature flag. Audited.

get.description: Radiology’s worklist (#96): the hospital’s imaging orders not cancelled or completed, at one stage, of one modality and priority when asked. To schedule is stat first, then urgent, then routine, the oldest ordered first within each; scheduled is the soonest slot first; performed the longest waiting first; reported (#97) the newest signed first. Each names the patient (name, MRN and date of birth), the study as ordered, its modality and its study. `total` comes with the first page, except for reported, whose count only grows. Every row read is audited. Requires imagingStudy:read with the scope `all` (a narrower one sees nothing) and the radiology feature flag. Holds no patient term: a GET.

post.description: Schedules the study of an imaging order for a slot, or moves it to another (#96). The first time makes the study, with the modality of its service as it is now, and accepts the order if it was only placed; after that the study’s version is required (409 `conflict`). Refused once the study is performed, and for an order cancelled, completed or moved in progress (409 `invalid_transition`). Requires imagingStudy:schedule and the radiology feature flag. Emits `imaging.scheduled`. The Idempotency-Key header is required: a repeat changes nothing and answers with the study as it is now. Audited.

Requires imagingStudy:schedule and the radiology feature flag. Emits `imaging.unscheduled`. The Idempotency-Key header is required: a repeat changes nothing and answers with the study as it is now. Requires imagingStudy:perform and the radiology feature flag. Emits `imaging.performed`. The Idempotency-Key header is required: a repeat changes nothing and answers with the study as it is now. Anyone who may write reports edits the draft. Refused for a study not performed (409 `invalid_transition`) and once the report is signed (409 `report_signed`). A link is https with no credentials (400 `invalid_link`); a template is an imaging report template of the hospital at that version (422 `template_not_found`). Requires imagingReport:write and imagingStudy:read with the scope `all` and the radiology feature flag. The Idempotency-Key header is required: a repeat changes nothing and answers with the report as it is now. Audited.

post.description: Signs the draft report of a study (#97) at the version sent (409 `conflict`): it never changes after, and its order is completed. The findings and the impression are needed (422 `report_incomplete`), and no placeholder of a template may be left unfilled in any part (422 `unfilled_placeholders`). Refused once signed (409 `report_signed`); 404 `report_not_found` with no draft. Requires imagingReport:sign and imagingStudy:read with the scope `all` and the radiology feature flag. Emits `imaging.reported`, and the order’s `order.completed`. The Idempotency-Key header is required: a repeat changes nothing and answers with the report as it is now. Audited.
